body:
## Why

The keepalive loop stops a PR with `stop (tasks-complete)` while unchecked task boxes are
visibly present in the PR body. Work then sits unclaimed behind a status line that says it is
finished — the same failure shape as #3433, in the reporting rather than the dispatch.

Measured 2026-09-14 on four PRs simultaneously:

| PR | Unchecked boxes in body | Loop's verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `stranske/Deliverable-Render` #14 | 1 of 23 | `stop (tasks-complete)` |
| `stranske/Ready` #570 | 2 of 7 | `stop (tasks-complete)` |

The loop's own state recorded `tasks: {"total": 5, "unchecked": 0}` for Ready #570 at a moment
when the body held nine `- [ ]` lines, four of them unchecked.

## Root cause (as far as I traced it)

Task accounting reads only the `- [ ]` lines inside the machine-owned
`<!-- auto-status-summary -->` block, which the summary job regenerates from the **source
issue**. Two consequences, both surprising:

1. Tasks added anywhere else in the PR body are invisible to the loop, however plainly a human
   or a reviewer wrote them.
2. Tasks written *into* the summary block are silently discarded on the next regeneration.

So the only durable way to add work to an in-flight PR is to edit the source issue and wait for
a `pr-meta` refresh. That is a reasonable design, but nothing says so, and the failure mode is
silent: the boxes appear in the body, a human sees unfinished work, and the loop reports
completion.

## Non-goals

- Making the PR body writable by hand. The summary block being machine-owned is fine.

## Tasks

- [ ] Count unchecked tasks across the whole PR body, not only inside the summary block — or,
      if that is deliberate, make the loop say so: `tasks-complete (summary block); N unchecked
      outside it`. A status must not read as "finished" while it is ignoring visible work.
- [ ] Preserve task lines added outside the summary block across a `pr-meta` regeneration
      instead of dropping them.
- [ ] Document the actual contract in `docs/keepalive/GoalsAndPlumbing.md`: the source issue is
      the task of record, the summary block is derived, and edits to either propagate only on a
      `pr-meta` refresh.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Named test: a PR body with an unchecked task outside the summary block does not yield
      `tasks-complete`.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** restore whole-body counting to summary-only → the new test
      **must FAIL** → revert.

## Implementation notes

The counter and the `tasks-complete` stop reason are in
`.github/scripts/keepalive_loop.js` (consumer copy under `templates/consumer-repo/`); the
regeneration is the `pr-meta` handler in `.github/workflows/agents-80-pr-event-hub.yml`.

Found while feeding adversarial-review findings back into four in-flight agent PRs. The
findings could not reach the agents until they were written into the source issues, and three
of those PRs had already reported themselves complete with the work undone — one of them
carrying `automerge`.

## Review follow-up on #3444 (2026-09-14)

- [ ] `visibleChecklistContent` strips HTML comments before recognising code fences (`.github/scripts/issue_scope_parser.js:17-26`), so a literal `<!--` inside a fenced block consumes every line through the next `-->` — including a genuine visible task. Extract fenced regions first, or use a Markdown-aware scanner.
- [ ] Add the counterexample as a regression test: a fenced `<!--`, then an unchecked task outside the fence, then `-->`. The task must be counted.
- [ ] Make the closed-comment / fence-only tests in `agents-pr-meta-update-body.test.js:1631-1635` discriminate the new behaviour from the old; today they pass under both.
